state.task: Quality control of peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) from one shotgun-proteomics run. Each question describes one PSM. Judge whether the peptide the search engine assigned is the peptide that produced the spectrum.
state.sample: Human HEK293T (293T) cell lysate. Proteins reduced with DTT, alkylated with iodoacetamide, digested with Lys-C and then trypsin; peptides separated into 24 basic-pH reversed-phase fractions. This run is one of those fractions.
state.acquisition: Thermo Q Exactive, nano-LC with a 3 h gradient, data-dependent top-20 method. MS1 in the Orbitrap at 70,000 resolution (300-1500 m/z). MS2 by HCD, 2 m/z isolation window, read in the Orbitrap at 17,500 resolution; centroided spectra. 55,352 MS2 spectra in the run.
state.search: Sage 0.14.6. Database: 20,416 human and 16,345 Arabidopsis thaliana SwissProt proteins plus reversed decoy sequences. No plant material is in the sample, so a match to an Arabidopsis-only or a decoy sequence is necessarily wrong. Trypsin (after K/R, not before P), up to 2 missed cleavages, peptide length 6-30, peptide mass 500-5000 Da; fixed carbamidomethyl-Cys, variable Met oxidation (max 2); precursor and fragment tolerance 10 ppm; isotope offsets -1 to +3; b and y ions, fragment charge up to 2; spectra deisotoped, 150 most intense peaks kept; only the top-ranked peptide per spectrum is reported.
state.listed_psms: All 46,191 top-ranked PSMs of the run are listed, unfiltered and in random order. From the number of decoy hits (9,130), about 40% of the listed PSMs are expected to be wrong and about 60% correct.
state.not_shown: Peptide sequence, protein, species and target/decoy status are withheld for every PSM. Judge from the match evidence.
state.how_to_read: A correct match usually explains the intense peaks of the spectrum with long contiguous b/y ladders (especially y); a false match typically matches many weak/noise peaks, scattered ions, few of the intense peaks. Buckets compare this PSM with all listed PSMs (1 = lowest, 10 = highest).
